chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from al-Makhzumi (and his mother was from the descendants of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib), who said:

Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) sent for us and gathered us, then said to us: Do you know why I have gathered you? We said: No. He said: Bear witness that this son of mine is my testamentary trustee (Wasi), the one who will uphold my affair, and my successor after me. Whoever has a debt from me, let him take it from this son of mine. Whoever has a promise from me, let him have it fulfilled from him. And whoever cannot do without meeting me, let him not meet me except through his letter.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Musa al-Kadhim designate his successor and manage his personal affairs?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the formal designation (Nass) of Imam al-Rida as the sole successor, emphasizing the continuity of authority through his son. The instruction to settle debts and promises through him underscores the transfer of spiritual and temporal rights, while the condition for future meetings via correspondence ('kitabu') points to the transition from physical presence to the era of the Minor and Major Gheyba. This event is pivotal in Shia scholarship for establishing the legitimacy of the eighth Imam's Imamate immediately following the seventh.
